title: Affine nonvanishing loci imply ampleness
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be a proper scheme over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $n\geq1$ and $s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$, put $X_s=\{x\in X:s_x\notin\mathfrak m_x(\mathcal L^{\otimes n})_x\}$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-residue-field]. If for every $x\in X$ there are $n\geq1$ and $s$ such that $x$ belongs to the affine open $X_s$, then $\mathcal L$ is ample in the sense of [def-sc-ample]: some positive tensor power of $\mathcal L$ has a complete linear system giving a closed immersion into projective space over $k$.

source.place: Properties, Definition 01PS (definition-ample): the affine nonvanishing-locus criterion; Morphisms, Lemma 01VT (lemma-finite-type-over-affine-ample-very-ample), (1) implies (5), with base Spec(k), using Lemma 01VK (lemma-ample-over-affine). Since X is proper and projective space is separated, the resulting immersion is closed. The complete-linear-system morphism is also a closed immersion: extend its finite defining sections to a basis of H^0(X,L^d), project back to the original linear system on the open where those coordinates do not simultaneously vanish, and use properness to make this immersion closed.

proof.text: Register properness and invertibility as instances. Properness makes X quasi-compact since Spec(k) is affine. For each x take the given positive power and section. The existing nonvanishing/local-generation equivalence identifies its generating open with its fibrewise nonvanishing locus. These affine opens therefore give Scheme.Modules.IsAmple X L.

Apply Scheme.Modules.IsAmple.exists_immersion_affine_base over k, using local finite type from properness. Obtain d>0 and an immersion i into finite projective space over k whose pullback of O(1) is the positive tensor power of L.

The finite projective space is proper, hence separated, over k. Since its composite with i equals f, IsProper.of_comp makes i proper. Its image is closed by universal closedness, so IsClosedImmersion.of_isPreimmersion makes i a closed immersion.

Identify the recursively defined positive tensor power with L.tensorPow d by induction: degree one uses the right unitor and each successor uses tensoring and symmetry. Identify tensorPullback i with Scheme.Modules.pullback i by uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward. Compose these isomorphisms with the immersion theorem's isomorphism, in the direction i*O(1) ≅ L.tensorPow d. The closed immersion, finite coordinate type and structure-morphism equality now directly witness IsVeryAmple f (L.tensorPow d); pair this with hL and d>0 to witness IsAmple f L.
